clue.text: Quite done for after the last punch

definitions.meaning: utterly ruined and destitute, with nothing left
a boxer knocked down and unable to rise is beaten in the ring

explanation.surface: A boxer is finished after taking the final blow of the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means destitute and finished, and in boxing describes a fighter floored and counted out.

clue.text: Command performance for very little money

definitions.meaning: an order to go ahead and act, as in an instruction to perform
a small old Dutch coin, hence a trifling sum

explanation.surface: A royal command performance is staged for a tiny fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'command' is the imperative telling someone to act; the coin sense survives in 'not worth a doit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken as an order it tells someone to perform, and as one word it names a tiny old Dutch coin.

clue.text: Scent to take one's breath away

definitions.meaning: in hunting, the smell of an animal carried on the air is its scent
a blow to the stomach can leave someone gasping and breathless

explanation.surface: A perfume so strong that it leaves one gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds catch the odour of game on the air, and a punch to the midriff can knock out a person's breath.

clue.text: The answer to the Celebes oil mess.

definitions.text: The answer to the Celebes oil mess.

parts.words: The answer to the Celebes oil mess.
parts.note: Macassar hair oil, named after a port in the Celebes, stained chair backs, and a cloth was devised against it

explanation.surface: A solution is sought for an oil spill in the Celebes.
explanation.walkthrough: Celebes is the old name of Sulawesi, whose port Makassar gave its name to a Victorian hair oil; the protective cloth laid over chair backs was named as being against it.
explanation.definitionFit: This chair-back cover was made to stop greasy hair oil from soiling upholstery.

clue.text: Poor scholar may pester church for money

parts.note: to dun is to pester a debtor for payment, which is why the clue adds 'for money'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A struggling student might badger the church for funds.
explanation.walkthrough: To dun is specifically to press for payment of money owed, so 'for money' completes the sense of 'pester'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull pupil, slow at learning, was traditionally made to wear a conical cap.

clue.text: Its larger version points to its constant star

definitions.text: Its larger version points to its constant star

parts.words: Its larger version points to its constant star
parts.note: the two pointer stars of the Great Bear lead the eye to the Pole Star, which lies in a smaller constellation

explanation.surface: Something's bigger model directs one towards a fixed star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough in the Great Bear has two 'pointers' that line up with Polaris, the near-constant Pole Star at the tip of the Little Bear's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Little Bear constellation, which holds the Pole Star; the Great Bear is the larger version.

clue.text: Knocks are returned when we do so in the ring

indicators.note: returned means the word for knocks is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: raps are knocks, as on a door

explanation.surface: Boxers trade blows that come back at them when they fight in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are returned' turns RAPS round to give SPAR; the surface's knocks sound like punches traded in boxing, which keeps the reader inside the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice, which is what fighters do in a ring.

clue.text: When the old are schooled by the young

definitions.text: When the old are schooled by the young

parts.words: When the old are schooled by the young
parts.note: on a school open day mothers and fathers visit and are shown round by their children

explanation.surface: An occasion when the young teach their elders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is slang for mother and father, and they are 'schooled' because they spend the day at school.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the school occasion when mothers and fathers visit to see their children's work and teachers.

clue.text: After card-games, actor gets commercial plant

parts.note: a rubber is a set of games at bridge or whist
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: After an evening of bridge, a performer comes into a business plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the actor second; Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated English actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The latex from this plant is tapped for industry, so it is grown as a cash crop.

clue.text: Quality of original sin-from a roadhouse at East Cape

parts.note: a roadhouse is a wayside inn
taken as written
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A theological quality seems to be traced to a pub at some eastern headland.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS, a headland, is common in British place names such as Orford Ness; here it is the cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Original sin is held to be inborn in every person, so its quality is being inherent from birth.

clue.text: Caught by Robert in Scotland, when rowing?

definitions.text: Caught by Robert in Scotland, when rowing?

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Rab is the Scottish short form of Robert

explanation.surface: A Scotsman called Robert is caught out while out on the water in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'catch a crab' is a rowing blunder in which the oar blade jams in the water, so the whole clue describes what is caught when rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a crab is the rowing term for an oar stroke that fouls in the water and jerks the rower.

clue.text: In a glow, having royal Peruvian forebears ?

definitions.meaning: split as two words, the pre-conquest rulers of Peru plus ancestry

explanation.surface: Someone flushed with pride claims kings of Peru as ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into INCA DESCENT: being descended from the Incas, Peru's royal line.
explanation.definitionFit: Shining with heat is the plain meaning, and split it describes ancestry from Peru's old rulers.

clue.text: Temporary nature of REME Camp Nine perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the three words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An army engineers' camp numbered nine seems to have been only a short-lived posting.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army; 'perhaps' rearranges REME CAMP NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being temporary rather than lasting is the condition of not being permanent.

clue.text: Tirades in classic battle with Civil Service

parts.note: Philippi in Macedonia was where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius in 42 BC

explanation.surface: An ancient battle sparks angry speeches among government officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon gave the word for a bitter verbal attack.

clue.text: No hasty proposal on film

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting; one that is far from quick, and the cinema technique of slowed-down action

explanation.surface: A screen proposal of marriage that takes its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposal' reads as a motion at a meeting; on film the phrase is the slowed-down replay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the film technique that shows action slower than life, and literally a motion that is unhurried.

clue.text: Coin of William or Mary ?

parts.note: William III and Mary II reigned jointly, so each monarch held only a share of the throne; read as an old British coin name

explanation.surface: A collector asks about a coin minted under William and Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: The half crown was an old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; William and Mary shared one crown, so each had half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a British silver coin of the pre-decimal currency, and also a fair description of a joint monarch's share.

clue.text: Crafty scholar gets, in one, thousand dollars for a few rulers

indicators.note: in says the two short pieces go inside the rearranged word
crafty says the letters of scholar are worked cunningly into a new shape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G, short for a grand, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A cunning academic pockets a thousand dollars to serve a small ruling clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' rearranges SCHOLAR into OLARCHS, and 'in' puts I and G inside it after OL.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a small group that holds power are this, from the Greek for rule by few.

clue.text: Some pass etching as valuable property

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An art dealer passes on an etching as if it were a treasured possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something owned that has value is called this in accounting and everyday speech.

clue.text: Sinclair is Harris's neighbour

definitions.meaning: the American novelist Sinclair, author of Main Street and Babbitt, had this surname
on the Scottish island of the Outer Hebrides, the northern part is joined to Harris

explanation.surface: A man called Sinclair turns out to live next door to someone called Harris.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris form one island of the Outer Hebrides off north-west Scotland; Lewis is its northern part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinclair Lewis was the Nobel-winning American novelist, and Lewis adjoins Harris on the same Hebridean island.

clue.text: Angry about organization of raid? Throw light on this

indicators.note: about says the word for angry goes round the other piece

parts.note: irate means angry

indicators.note: organization says the letters of the word raid are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone furious about how a raid was organised wants it exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization of' rearranges RAID into RADI, which 'about' puts inside IRATE after its IR.
explanation.definitionFit: To irradiate something is to shine light or radiation upon it.

clue.text: Missionary for heathen district ?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pagan is a heathen

explanation.surface: A missionary is sent out to a region of unbelievers.
explanation.definitionFit: A missionary spreads a creed, and someone who spreads a doctrine is its zealous promoter.

clue.text: Force a way to the door

definitions.meaning: to compel or push someone, as in driving them to act
a private road leading up to a house

explanation.surface: Someone is pushed along a path up to the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel is to push someone on, and the private road from street to house has the same name.

clue.text: Oats mashed in the porch

indicators.note: mashed says the letters of oats are pulped into a new order

explanation.surface: Porridge oats are being mashed on the front porch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Painted Porch in Athens, where Zeno taught, giving the Stoics their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Misfortunes of Cockney, at Tower-and Ludgate ?:

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the letter at the start of words, so the h goes

parts.note: Tower Hill and Ludgate Hill are both London hills

explanation.surface: A Cockney's troubles are located at two London landmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, drop their aitches; Tower Hill and Ludgate Hill are London streets, so 'HILLS becomes 'ILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles and misfortunes are both called ills, as in the ills of the world.

clue.text: Flag gives colour to the eye

definitions.meaning: a flag is a plant of the genus with sword-shaped leaves, the yellow flag being one
the ring of tissue round the pupil gives an eye its colour

explanation.surface: A banner lends its colours to the scene before one's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag is a common name for this flowering plant, and the same word names the coloured part of the eye.

clue.text: Old accent I reproduce for Western

indicators.note: reproduce says the letters given are produced again in a different order

explanation.surface: An actor imitates an old accent to play a cowboy in a Western.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from the Latin for the setting sun, so it means of the West.

clue.text: Forwarded perfume, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and another spelling heard

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the perfume was passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent and forwarded both mean dispatched onward to someone else.

clue.text: Bare ones for tanners being a sunny day and a high wall ?. .

definitions.text: Bare ones for tanners being a sunny day and a high wall ?

parts.words: Bare ones for tanners being a sunny day and a high wall ?
parts.note: read as the minimum things a naked sunbather needs: sun to tan and a wall for privacy, the idiom of the bare basics

explanation.surface: A sunbather lists what a nude tan requires: sunshine and a tall wall for privacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare' plays on the idiom of the bare necessities and on the sunbather being naked; the tanners are sunbathers, not leather workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The things one cannot do without are the indispensable basics, and 'the bare ones' is a fixed idiom.
